albums.blurb: Dungen are the Stockholm psychedelic rock band led by multi-instrumentalist Gustav Ejstes, singing in Swedish since the late 1990s and best known abroad for 2004's Ta Det Lugnt. Häxan, released on Mexican Summer in November 2016, is their first all-instrumental record: a fourteen-track score commissioned for Lotte Reiniger's 1926 silhouette animation The Adventures of Prince Achmed, the oldest surviving animated feature film, which the band has performed live to screenings.
albums.reception: It holds a Metacritic score of 76 ("generally favorable") from six critic reviews, with AllMusic writing that the score "stands alone as a sterling example of the band's mastery of psychedelic music."

albums.album: If This Isn't Nice, I Don't Know What Is
albums.blurb: Still Woozy is Sven Gamsky, a Bay Area producer and songwriter who left the math-rock band Feed Me Jack and spent four years building an audience one self-recorded single at a time. This 2021 Interscope release, co-produced with Lars Stalfors, is his debut full-length, gathering thirteen short tracks of woozy, homespun funk-pop that fold in earlier singles like "Rocky" and "Window".
albums.reception: The album peaked at No. 150 on the Billboard 200, Gamsky's first appearance on that chart.

albums.blurb: Bobbie Gentry, the Mississippi-born singer-songwriter who topped the charts in 1967 with "Ode to Billie Joe", followed it in February 1968 with this Capitol concept album: a song cycle about her Delta upbringing in Chickasaw County that threads her own vignettes like "Okolona River Bottom Band" between swampy covers of "Big Boss Man", "Parchman Farm" and "Tobacco Road". A deluxe reissue with new stereo mixes appeared in 2020.
albums.reception: A commercial disappointment that stalled at No. 132 on the Billboard albums chart on release, it has since been reappraised — The Guardian called it "a lost masterpiece" in 2013, and Mercury Rev re-recorded it song for song on 2019's Bobbie Gentry's The Delta Sweete Revisited.
